newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Spendrups says PepsiCo wants new contract.
newsitem.headline: Spendrups says PepsiCo wants new contract.

text.p: Swedish beverage maker Spendrups said on Tuesday that PepsiCo wanted to renegotiate the forms for cooperation with Spendrup's Norwegian subsidiary Christianssands Bryggeri.
"PepsiCo has announced that it does not automatically wish to renew the cooperation with our Norwegian subsidiary Christianssands Bryggeri after December 15 1998," Spendrups said in a statement.
"The reason is that it wants to renegotiate the forms for cooperation and we will start negotiations shortly," it said.
Spendrups and Christianssands Bryggeri have boosted sales of PepsiCo's products to "very high market shares in an international perspective", the company said.
In Sweden, PepsiCo's market share is 25 percent and in southern Norway it is close to 30 percent, Spendrups said.
"We are convinced that it is in the interest of both parties that Christianssands Bryggeri keeps drawing and distributing Pepsi and we aim for a longterm cooperation with PepsiCo," the company said.
